ausparl

Query the Australian Hansard database from R.

Overview

ausparl gives basic, reproducible access to the Australian Parliamentary Hansard, the record of debates in the House of Representatives and the Senate since 1901, held in a pre-built DuckDB database. With it you can:

  • filter sittings, speeches and speaking turns by member, party, parliament, chamber and date;
  • search speeches for words and phrases, with hit counts;
  • add what was true of the speaker on the day (party, role, electorate, age, government or opposition);
  • look up members: their service, parties, ministerial roles and background;
  • summarise activity per member, party and parliament;
  • hand results to quanteda for text analysis.

Queries run inside the database and only the results come back into R. The database is opened read-only.

Installation

Install ausparl from GitHub with remotes:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Australian-Parliamentary-Speech/ausparl")

To install a particular release, name its tag:

remotes::install_github("Australian-Parliamentary-Speech/ausparl@v0.1.3")

This installs the package and the packages it depends on, including duckdb and quanteda. R 4.1 or later is required. The Hansard database itself (about 9.5 GB) is separate: it is not installed with the package, and it is never loaded into memory, because ausparl queries it on disk.

Getting the database

Download it. db_download() installs the database version this release of ausparl uses (see Versions), checks its checksum, and resumes an interrupted download when run again. By default it goes in your R user data directory, and db_connect() with no arguments then opens it:

library(ausparl)
db_download()
db_connect()

Keep working while it downloads. db_download(background = TRUE) runs the download in the background: as a job in RStudio’s Background Jobs pane, or elsewhere in a separate R process that keeps going if you close R. Connect once it has finished.

Download it into a folder of your own, such as the dataset/ folder of a clone of this repository. From that folder (or the one above dataset/), db_connect() finds it by itself; from anywhere else, open it by path:

db_download(dir = "dataset")
db_connect(path = "dataset/hansard.duckdb")

Use a copy you already have. Pass its path, db_connect(path = "/path/to/hansard.duckdb"), or set it once in ~/.Renviron so that db_connect() finds it in every session:

AUSPARL_DB=/path/to/hansard.duckdb

You can open that file with usethis::edit_r_environ(); restart R after saving it. A path you pass comes first, then AUSPARL_DB, then the copy db_download() installed in the user data directory, then the full database you opened earlier in the session, then hansard.duckdb in the working directory or its dataset/ folder.

Try it with the bundled sample (eight sitting days, no download needed):

db_connect(sample = TRUE)

Example 

library(ausparl)
library(dplyr)
db_connect(sample = TRUE)

db_info()                                     # which database, which version

howard <- find_member("john howard")$PHID     # a member's identifier
member_profile(howard)$ministry_records       # their ministerial roles

# Speeches per parliament, counted inside the database
get_speeches(include_text = FALSE, collect = FALSE) |>
  count(parliament_id, chamber) |>
  arrange(parliament_id, chamber) |>
  collect()

# Mentions of a word by year
search_speeches_by_terms("government", include_text = FALSE, collect = FALSE) |>
  group_by(year = year(date)) |>
  summarise(n_turns = n(), n_mentions = sum(n_hits, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(year) |>
  collect()

# A member's speeches, with their role on the day, as a quanteda corpus
get_speeches(member = howard, limit = 20) |>
  add_role() |>
  as_corpus()

db_disconnect()

vignette("database") describes the database itself: its tables, identifiers, turn types, speaker matching and provenance. For a first analysis, see the worked example below. The package help page, ?ausparl, lists the functions by task and the package options.

The documentation is also online at https://australian-parliamentary-speech.github.io/ausparl/.

Example code

The example/ folder of this repository holds a worked example: a short, runnable tour of the database and the package, from connecting to handing speeches to quanteda. To run it, clone or download this repository and, from its top folder, either render example/walkthrough.qmd with Quarto (quarto render example/walkthrough.qmd) or run the plain R version, source("example/walkthrough.R"). It uses the full database in dataset/ if you have downloaded it there with ausparl::db_download(dir = "dataset"), and otherwise the sample bundled with the package. Details are in example/README.md.

Main functions

Most query functions take collect (TRUE returns a tibble; FALSE a lazy table you can keep filtering and summarising in the database), limit and columns. Interjections are left out of speech results unless you ask for them.

Area Functions
Connection db_download(), db_connect(), db_disconnect(), db_info(), db_con(), db_tbl()
Speeches and search get_speeches(), get_speech_turns(), search_speeches_by_terms(), get_sitting_timeline(), get_interjections()
Members find_member(), member_profile()
Activity summaries member_activity(), party_activity(), parliament_summary()
Context on the day add_party(), add_role(), add_government_status(), add_electorate(), add_age(), add_member(), add_debate()
Tables get_sittings(), get_debates(), get_subdebates(), get_actions(), get_members(), get_parliaments(), get_parties(), get_party_service(), get_parl_service(), get_electorates(), get_elections(), get_ministries(), get_ministry_records(), get_shadow_ministry_records(), get_committee_members(), get_presiding_officers(), get_occupations(), get_qualifications(), get_schools(), get_provenance()
Filter helpers in_range(), matches_pattern()
Outputs as_corpus(), result_provenance()

See ?function_name for the arguments of each function.

Versions

Each ausparl release uses one database version, and db_download() installs exactly that version.

ausparl Package DOI Database version Database DOI
0.1.3 10.5281/zenodo.24515972 7.0.0-20261123 10.5281/zenodo.24452577
0.1.2 10.5281/zenodo.24493556 7.0.0-20261123 10.5281/zenodo.24452577
0.1.1 10.5281/zenodo.24491242 7.0.0-20261123 10.5281/zenodo.24452577
0.1.0 none 7.0.0-20261123 10.5281/zenodo.24452577

Each release from 0.1.1 is archived on Zenodo with its own DOI. 10.5281/zenodo.24491241 covers all versions and always resolves to the latest.

Authors

Citation

If you use ausparl, please cite the version you used, and the database version it pins. For this release:

Leslie, P., Taflaga, M., Benoit, K., Alexander, R., Dowding, K. and Zhu, G. (2026). ausparl: Query the Australian Parliamentary Hansard Database. R package version 0.1.3. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24515972. Using Hansard database version 7.0.0-20261123 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24452577).

In R, citation("ausparl") gives the same citation for the version you have installed, with a BibTeX entry (toBibtex(citation("ausparl"))). GitHub’s Cite this repository button, built from CITATION.cff, gives it in APA and BibTeX.

For another version, find its DOI in the table under Versions, or on Zenodo. The citation records the package version and the database version it pins, with the database’s Zenodo DOI. Report the schema_version and built_at from db_info() as well.
